advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider scoping the census's `assignments` collection (or documenting the module-flat, last-writer-wins limitation) so future name-shadowing cannot silently mis-resolve `mode=`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_rp01_s5_authoritative_oracle.py:131: `assignments: dict[str, ast.AST] = {}` collected via a module-wide `ast.walk(tree)` with no scope tracking
tests/unit/test_rp01_s5_authoritative_oracle.py:117: `if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id in assignments:` resolves the flat, last-writer-wins binding
Currently sound: fidelity_spot_eval.py:101 binds `mode` once at module-visible scope and the test asserts explicit named files, so no mis-resolution occurs today.
advisory.finding: The mode-resolving census collects assignment bindings scope-blind: `_structured_consumer_files` walks the whole module tree and stores every single-target Name assignment into one flat `assignments` dict, so if a variable named `mode` (or any resolved name) is reassigned in a different function/scope, the last-walked binding wins and could mis-resolve a `mode=` argument. Today it is safe because of the explicit named-file anchor assertions and the >=10 margin, but the mechanism is fragile to future consumers that shadow such names.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-anchor the single-source AC-1 check to observable behavior (or downgrade to a lint) rather than asserting hardcoded internal identifier names / filenames parsed from source under test.
evidence: The assertion targets identifier text and filenames parsed from src/rebar and scripts (source under test), not any observable runtime behavior; it satisfies the refactoring-violation criterion (a).
advisory.finding: AC-1 single-source test asserts on internal implementation identifier names and module filenames grepped from source code under test, making it a change-detector/source-grep: a behavior-preserving rename of `_pai_structured`/`_run_native_output`/`_run_prompted_output`, or relocating the runner dispatch into a new helper module, breaks it with no observable-behavior change.
scenarios: A maintainer renames the private helpers or extracts a second dispatch module during a behavior-preserving refactor and this test fails spuriously.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the filename/`>=10` count assertions in the census-mechanism test with a behavior-anchored or fixture-driven check that does not break on consumer renames/consolidation.
evidence: assert len(files) >= 10, f"census under-counted structured consumers: {sorted(files)}"

The assertions are over filenames and a count derived by AST-grepping source under test; this verifies the census helper's own resolution logic and the current file inventory, not product behavior — a refactoring-violation (criterion a).
advisory.finding: AC-1 census-mechanism test asserts specific consumer FILENAMES (`fidelity_spot_eval.py`, `jira_dc_capability_map.py`) and a magic count `len(files) >= 10` over source, coupling the test to file layout and consumer count rather than observable behavior; renaming/moving a consumer file or legitimately consolidating consumers below 10 breaks it with no behavior change.
scenarios: A consumer file is renamed or two consumers are merged during refactor; the count/filename assertions fail though structured dispatch behavior is unchanged.
